verses.original: Ὁμοία γάρ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅστις ἐξῆλθεν ἅμα πρωῒ μισθώσασθαι ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Homoia gar estin hē basileia tōn ouranōn anthrōpō oikodespotē hostis exēlthen hama prōi misthōsasthai ergatas eis ton ampelōna autou
verses.literal: For the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard
verses.literalPt: Pois o reino dos céus é semelhante a um proprietário, que saiu de madrugada a assalariar trabalhadores para a sua vinha.

verses.original: συμφωνήσας δὲ μετὰ τῶν ἐργατῶν ἐκ δηναρίου τὴν ἡμέραν ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: symphōnēsas de meta tōn ergatōn ek dēnariou tēn hēmeran apesteilen autous eis ton ampelōna autou
verses.literal: He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard
verses.literalPt: Feito com os trabalhadores o ajuste de um denário por dia, mandou-os para a sua vinha.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν περὶ τρίτην ὥραν εἶδεν ἄλλους ἑστῶτας ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ ἀργούς
verses.transliteration: Kai exelthōn peri tritēn hōran eiden allous hestōtas en tē agora argous
verses.literal: About the third hour he went out and saw others standing in the marketplace doing nothing
verses.literalPt: Tendo saído cerca da hora terceira, viu estarem outros na praça desocupados,

verses.original: καὶ ἐκείνοις εἶπεν Ὑπάγετε καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα καὶ ὃ ἐὰν ᾖ δίκαιον δώσω ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: kai ekeinois eipen Hypagete kai hymeis eis ton ampelōna kai ho ean ē dikaion dōsō hymin
verses.literal: You also go into my vineyard he said and I will pay you whatever . . . is right
verses.literalPt: e disse-lhes: Ide também vós para a minha vinha, e vos darei o que for justo. Eles foram.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἀπῆλθον Πάλιν δὲ ἐξελθὼν περὶ ἕκτην καὶ ἐνάτην ὥραν ἐποίησεν ὡσαύτως
verses.transliteration: hoi de apēlthon Palin de exelthōn peri hektēn kai enatēn hōran epoiēsen hōsautōs
verses.literal: So they went He went out again about the sixth hour and the ninth hour and did the same thing
verses.literalPt: Saiu outra vez cerca da hora sexta e da nona, e fez o mesmo.

verses.original: Περὶ δὲ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην ἐξελθὼν εὗρεν ἄλλους ἑστῶτας καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Τί ὧδε ἑστήκατε ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἀργοί
verses.transliteration: Peri de tēn hendekatēn exelthōn heuren allous hestōtas kai legei autois Ti hōde hestēkate holēn tēn hēmeran argoi
verses.literal: About the eleventh hour he went out and found still others standing around Why have you been standing here all day long doing nothing he asked . . .
verses.literalPt: Cerca da undécima, saiu e achou outros que lá estavam, e perguntou-lhes: Por que estais aqui todo o dia desocupados?

verses.original: Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἡμᾶς ἐμισθώσατο Λέγει αὐτοῖς Ὑπάγετε καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα
verses.transliteration: Legousin autō Hoti oudeis hēmas emisthōsato Legei autois Hypagete kai hymeis eis ton ampelōna
verses.literal: Because no one has hired us they answered . . . So he told them You also go into my vineyard
verses.literalPt: Responderam-lhe: Porque ninguém nos assalariou. Disse-lhes: Ide também vós para a minha vinha.

verses.original: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης λέγει ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος τῷ ἐπιτρόπῳ αὐτοῦ Κάλεσον τοὺς ἐργάτας καὶ ἀπόδος αὐτοῖς τὸν μισθόν ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῶν ἐσχάτων ἕως τῶν πρώτων
verses.transliteration: Opsias de genomenēs legei ho kyrios tou ampelōnos tō epitropō autou Kaleson tous ergatas kai apodos autois ton misthon arxamenos apo tōn eschatōn heōs tōn prōtōn
verses.literal: When evening came the owner of the vineyard said to his foreman Call the workers and pay them their wages starting with the last ones hired and moving on to the first
verses.literalPt: À tarde disse o dono da vinha ao seu administrador: Chama os trabalhadores e paga-lhes o salário, começando pelos últimos e acabando pelos primeiros.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ περὶ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην ὥραν ἔλαβον ἀνὰ δηνάριον
verses.transliteration: Kai elthontes hoi peri tēn hendekatēn hōran elabon ana dēnarion
verses.literal: The workers who were hired about the eleventh hour came and each received a denarius
verses.literalPt: Tendo chegado os que tinham sido assalariados cerca da undécima hora, receberam um denário cada um.

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ πρῶτοι ἐνόμισαν ὅτι πλεῖον λήμψονται καὶ ἔλαβον τὸ ἀνὰ δηνάριον καὶ αὐτοί
verses.transliteration: kai elthontes hoi prōtoi enomisan hoti pleion lēmpsontai kai elabon to ana dēnarion kai autoi
verses.literal: So when the original workers came they assumed they would receive more But each of them also received a denarius
verses.literalPt: Vindo os primeiros, pensavam que haviam de receber mais; porém receberam igualmente um denário cada um.

verses.original: Λαβόντες δὲ ἐγόγγυζον κατὰ τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου
verses.transliteration: Labontes de egongyzon kata tou oikodespotou
verses.literal: On receiving their pay they began to grumble against the landowner
verses.literalPt: Ao receberem-no, murmuravam contra o proprietário,

verses.original: λέγοντες Οὗτοι οἱ ἔσχατοι μίαν ὥραν ἐποίησαν καὶ ἴσους αὐτοὺς ἡμῖν ἐποίησας τοῖς βαστάσασι τὸ βάρος τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸν καύσωνα
verses.transliteration: legontes Houtoi hoi eschatoi mian hōran epoiēsan kai isous autous hēmin epoiēsas tois bastasasi to baros tēs hēmeras kai ton kausōna
verses.literal: These men who were hired last worked only one hour they said and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden and the scorching heat of the day
verses.literalPt: alegando: Estes últimos trabalharam somente uma hora, e os igualaste a nós, que suportamos o peso do dia e o calor extremo.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς ἑνὶ αὐτῶν εἶπεν Ἑταῖρε οὐκ ἀδικῶ σε οὐχὶ δηναρίου συνεφώνησάς μοι
verses.transliteration: Ho de apokritheis heni autōn eipen Hetaire ouk adikō se ouchi dēnariou synephōnēsas moi
verses.literal: But he answered one of them Friend I am not being unfair to you Did you not agree with me on one denarius
verses.literalPt: Mas o proprietário disse a um deles: Meu amigo, não te faço injustiça; não ajustaste comigo um denário?

verses.original: ἆρον τὸ σὸν καὶ ὕπαγε θέλω δὲ τούτῳ τῷ ἐσχάτῳ δοῦναι ὡς καὶ σοί
verses.transliteration: aron to son kai hypage thelō de toutō tō eschatō dounai hōs kai soi
verses.literal: Take your pay and go I want to give this last man the same as I gave you
verses.literalPt: Toma o que é teu, e vai-te embora; pois quero dar a este último tanto como a ti.

verses.original: ἢ οὐκ ἔξεστίν μοι ὃ θέλω ποιῆσαι ἐν τοῖς ἐμοῖς ἢ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρός ἐστιν ὅτι ἐγὼ ἀγαθός εἰμι
verses.transliteration: ē ouk exestin moi ho thelō poiēsai en tois emois ē ho ophthalmos sou ponēros estin hoti egō agathos eimi
verses.literal: Do I not have the right . . . to do as I please with what is mine Or are you . . . . . . . . . envious because I am generous
verses.literalPt: Não me é lícito fazer o que me apraz do que é meu? Acaso o teu olho é mau, porque eu sou bom.

verses.original: Οὕτως ἔσονται οἱ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι
verses.transliteration: Houtōs esontai hoi eschatoi prōtoi kai hoi prōtoi eschatoi
verses.literal: So the last will be first and the first will be last
verses.literalPt: Assim os últimos serão primeiros, e os primeiros serão últimos.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀναβαίνων ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παρέλαβεν τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητὰς κατ’ ἰδίαν καὶ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: Kai anabainōn ho Iēsous eis Hierosolyma parelaben tous dōdeka mathētas kat’ idian kai en tē hodō eipen autois
verses.literal: As Jesus was going up - to Jerusalem He took the twelve disciples aside and said
verses.literalPt: Estando Jesus para subir a Jerusalém, chamou à parte os doze e, em caminho lhes disse:

verses.original: Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ γραμματεῦσιν καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν εἰς θανάτῳ
verses.transliteration: Idou anabainomen eis Hierosolyma kai ho Huios tou anthrōpou paradothēsetai tois archiereusin kai grammateusin kai katakrinousin auton eis thanatō
verses.literal: Look we are going up to Jerusalem and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes They will condemn Him to death
verses.literalPt: Eis que subimos a Jerusalém, e o Filho do Homem será entregue aos principais sacerdotes e aos escribas; eles o condenarão à morte

verses.original: καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν εἰς τὸ ἐμπαῖξαι καὶ μαστιγῶσαι καὶ σταυρῶσαι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθήσεται
verses.transliteration: kai paradōsousin auton tois ethnesin eis to empaixai kai mastigōsai kai staurōsai kai tē tritē hēmera egerthēsetai
verses.literal: and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles to be mocked and flogged and crucified And on the third day He will be raised to life
verses.literalPt: e o entregarão aos gentios para ser escarnecido, açoitado e crucificado, e ao terceiro dia ressuscitará.

verses.original: Τότε προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου μετὰ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῆς προσκυνοῦσα καὶ αἰτοῦσά τι ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Tote prosēlthen autō hē mētēr tōn huiōn Zebedaiou meta tōn huiōn autēs proskynousa kai aitousa ti ap’ autou
verses.literal: Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons and knelt down to make a request . . . of Him
verses.literalPt: Então se chegou a ele a mulher de Zebedeu com seus filhos, adorando-o e pedindo-lhe um favor.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Τί θέλεις Λέγει αὐτῷ Εἰπὲ ἵνα καθίσωσιν οὗτοι οἱ δύο υἱοί μου εἷς ἐκ δεξιῶν σου καὶ εἷς ἐξ εὐωνύμων σου ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ σου
verses.transliteration: Ho de eipen autē Ti theleis Legei autō Eipe hina kathisōsin houtoi hoi dyo huioi mou heis ek dexiōn sou kai heis ex euōnymōn sou en tē basileia sou
verses.literal: What do you want - He inquired She answered . . . Declare that in Your kingdom one of these two sons of mine may sit at Your right hand and the other at Your left
verses.literalPt: Jesus perguntou-lhe: Que queres? Ela respondeu: Manda que estes meus dois filhos se assentem, um à tua direita, e outro à tua esquerda, no teu reino.

verses.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ μέλλω πίνειν Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Δυνάμεθα
verses.transliteration: Apokritheis de ho Iēsous eipen Ouk oidate ti aiteisthe dynasthe piein to potērion ho egō mellō pinein Legousin autō Dynametha
verses.literal: You do not know what you are asking - Jesus replied Can you drink the cup I am going to drink We can the brothers answered . . .
verses.literalPt: Mas ele replicou: Não sabeis o que pedis. Podeis beber o cálice que eu estou para beber? Responderam eles: Podemos:

verses.original: Λέγει αὐτοῖς Τὸ μὲν ποτήριόν μου πίεσθε τὸ δὲ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μου καὶ ἐξ εὐωνύμων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν τοῦτο δοῦναι ἀλλ’ οἷς ἡτοίμασται ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατρός μου
verses.transliteration: Legei autois To men potērion mou piesthe to de kathisai ek dexiōn mou kai ex euōnymōn ouk estin emon touto dounai all’ hois hētoimastai hypo tou Patros mou
verses.literal: You will indeed drink My cup Jesus said But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant These seats belong to those for whom My Father has prepared them
verses.literalPt: Ele lhes disse: Na verdade, haveis de beber o meu cálice; mas o tomar assento à minha direita ou à minha esquerda não me pertence concedê-lo, porém será dado àqueles para quem está destinado por meu Pai.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα ἠγανάκτησαν περὶ τῶν δύο ἀδελφῶν
verses.transliteration: Kai akousantes hoi deka ēganaktēsan peri tōn dyo adelphōn
verses.literal: When the ten heard about this they were indignant with the two brothers
verses.literalPt: Ouvindo isso os dez, indignaram-se contra os dois irmãos.

verses.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς εἶπεν Οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἄρχοντες τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: ho de Iēsous proskalesamenos autous eipen Oidate hoti hoi archontes tōn ethnōn katakyrieuousin autōn kai hoi megaloi katexousiazousin autōn
verses.literal: But Jesus called them aside . . . and said You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them and their superiors exercise authority over them
verses.literalPt: Mas Jesus chamou-os a si e disse: Sabeis que os governadores dos gentios dominam os seus vassalos, e sobre eles os grandes exercem autoridade.

verses.original: οὐχ οὕτως ἔσται ἐν ὑμῖν ἀλλ’ ὃς ἐὰν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν μέγας γενέσθαι ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος
verses.transliteration: ouch houtōs estai en hymin all’ hos ean thelē en hymin megas genesthai estai hymōn diakonos
verses.literal: It shall not be this way among you Instead whoever . . . wants to become great among you must be your servant
verses.literalPt: Não é assim entre vós. Mas quem quiser tornar-se grande entre vós, será esse o que vos sirva;

verses.original: καὶ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι πρῶτος ἔσται ὑμῶν δοῦλος
verses.transliteration: kai hos an thelē en hymin einai prōtos estai hymōn doulos
verses.literal: and whoever . . . wants to be first among you must be your slave
verses.literalPt: e quem quiser ser o primeiro entre vós, será esse o vosso servo.

verses.original: ὥσπερ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν
verses.transliteration: hōsper ho Huios tou anthrōpou ouk ēlthen diakonēthēnai alla diakonēsai kai dounai tēn psychēn autou lytron anti pollōn
verses.literal: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve and to give His life as a ransom for many
verses.literalPt: É assim que o Filho do Homem não veio para ser servido, mas para servir e dar a sua vida em resgate de muitos.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Ἰεριχὼ ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς
verses.transliteration: Kai ekporeuomenōn autōn apo Ierichō ēkolouthēsen autō ochlos polys
verses.literal: As they were leaving . . . Jericho a large crowd followed Him
verses.literalPt: Saindo eles de Jericó, acompanhou a Jesus uma grande multidão.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο τυφλοὶ καθήμενοι παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Ἰησοῦς παράγει ἔκραξαν λέγοντες Κύριε ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς υἱὸς Δαυίδ
verses.transliteration: kai idou dyo typhloi kathēmenoi para tēn hodon akousantes hoti Iēsous paragei ekraxan legontes Kyrie eleēson hēmas huios Dauid
verses.literal: And there were two blind men sitting beside the road When they heard that Jesus was passing by they cried out . . . Lord Son of David have mercy on us
verses.literalPt: Dois cegos, sentados à beira do caminho, sabendo que Jesus passava, clamaram: Senhor, filho de Davi, tem compaixão de nós!

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ ὄχλος ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα σιωπήσωσιν οἱ δὲ μεῖζον ἔκραξαν λέγοντες Κύριε ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς υἱὸς Δαυίδ
verses.transliteration: Ho de ochlos epetimēsen autois hina siōpēsōsin hoi de meizon ekraxan legontes Kyrie eleēson hēmas huios Dauid
verses.literal: The crowd admonished them to be silent but they cried out all the louder Lord Son of David have mercy on us
verses.literalPt: A multidão mandou que se calassem, mas eles clamavam cada vez mais: Tem compaixão de nós, Senhor, filho de Davi!

verses.original: Καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐφώνησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ εἶπεν Τί θέλετε ποιήσω ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: Kai stas ho Iēsous ephōnēsen autous kai eipen Ti thelete poiēsō hymin
verses.literal: Jesus stopped and called them What do you want Me to do for you He asked
verses.literalPt: Jesus, parando, chamou-os e perguntou-lhes: Que desejais que eu vos faça?

verses.original: Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Κύριε ἵνα ἀνοιγῶσιν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἡμῶν
verses.transliteration: Legousin autō Kyrie hina anoigōsin hoi ophthalmoi hēmōn
verses.literal: Lord they answered . . . let our eyes be opened
verses.literalPt: Responderam: Senhor, que se nos abram os olhos.

verses.original: Σπλαγχνισθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἥψατο τῶν ὀμμάτων αὐτῶν καὶ εὐθέως ἀνέβλεψαν καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: Splanchnistheis de ho Iēsous hēpsato tōn ommatōn autōn kai eutheōs aneblepsan kai ēkolouthēsan autō
verses.literal: Moved with compassion Jesus touched their eyes and at once they received their sight and followed Him
verses.literalPt: Jesus, condoído, tocou-lhes os olhos; no mesmo instante, recuperaram a vista e seguiram-no.
